title: 1980 AHSME Problem 22
statement: For each real number \(x,\) let \(f(x)\) be the minimum of the numbers \(4x+1,\) \(x+2,\) and \(-2x+4.\) Then the maximum value of \(f(x)\) is

solutions.text:
The lower envelope is \(4x+1\) until it meets \(x+2\) at \(x=\frac{1}{3},\) then is \(x+2\) until that line meets \(-2x+4\) at \(x=\frac{2}{3},\) and thereafter is \(-2x+4.\) Thus its maximum occurs at \(x=\frac{2}{3}\) and equals \[ \frac23+2=\frac83. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Sketch the three lines and follow their lower envelope
The maximum occurs where the active increasing line meets the decreasing line
